extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, facility environmental consultants, state regulators, and attorneys involved in CCR compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory definitions for identifying when a coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundment at an inactive facility qualifies as a legacy CCR surface impoundment (i.e., 'contains both CCR and liquids'), how 'liquids' are defined, the dewatering standard, and the methods and evidence EPA expects to evaluate presence/absence of free liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a legacy CCR surface impoundment
rubrics_metrics.description: A legacy CCR surface impoundment is defined as a CCR surface impoundment at an inactive facility that "contains both CCR and liquid," consistent with the discussion in the proposal and the dewatering standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition incorporates the dictionary meaning of 'contains' and relies on the dewatering standard to determine whether a unit contains liquids. EPA explains that many units that have been 'dewatered' in practice still retain free liquids (e.g., porewater, water from rainfall) and therefore may meet the definition. The regulation applies to current owners/operators; if only standing water was removed as of October 19, 2015, the unit may still be subject to the rule. EPA provided a definition in §257.53 that codifies this construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'liquids'
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquids means any fluid (such as water) that has no independent shape but has a definite volume and does not expand indefinitely and that is only slightly compressible; encompasses water sluiced into the impoundment, precipitation, surface water, groundwater, free water, standing water ponded above CCR, and porewater intermingled with CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA adopted a Merriam-Webster-based plain-language definition in §257.53 and declined to adopt the proposal's technical definition or the Paint Filter Liquids Test-based definition. The definition is intended to make clear that all kinds of water are relevant to determining applicability. EPA rejected alternatives because of potential confusion (e.g., fly ash behavior), technical measurement difficulties, and sampling artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contains both CCR and liquids (regulatory formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contains both CCR and liquids means that both CCR and liquids are present in a CCR surface impoundment, except where the owner or operator demonstrates that the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) has been met."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formulation ties the 'contains' determination to an affirmative demonstration under the dewatering standard. EPA places the burden on owners/operators to show the standard is met; absent such demonstration, the unit is regulated as containing liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR surface impoundment statutory criteria (§257.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing definition in §257.53 contains three criteria: (1) unit is a natural topographic depression, manmade excavation or diked area; (2) unit is designed to hold an accumulation of CCR and liquid; and (3) unit treats, stores or disposes of CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of these criteria require the presence of a particular amount of water or hydraulic head. Whether a unit is a surface impoundment is determined by these design/use criteria, not by transient presence of small amounts of water (e.g., rainfall that is readily absorbed). Indicators that a unit is not a surface impoundment include evidence it was constructed or operated for dry CCR placement (e.g., leachate collection meeting §257.70(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dewatering standard (§257.102(d)(2)(i)) as basis for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may demonstrate that the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) has been met to show an impoundment does not 'contain' liquids for purposes of the legacy definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of free liquids is treated as an affirmative defense; EPA recommends facilities develop and retain records supporting any determination that the exception applies. EPA provided additional time in the final rule for facilities to determine elimination of free liquids as part of the applicability report. EPA also issued a memorandum summarizing methods and tools to determine whether free liquids have been eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement/identification tools for free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools currently used to identify free liquids include soil borings and cone penetrometers to map stratigraphy and characterize geotechnical/hydraulic properties, installation of traditional piezometers, monitoring wells, and vibrating wire piezometers to monitor pore pressures and water levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly constructed and screened wells/piezometers directly measure water levels under ambient conditions and are indicative of free liquids at that location. EPA recommends a holistic evaluation of all site-wide monitoring data (e.g., piezometers, vibrating wire piezometers) and monitoring networks with sufficient point density to independently verify dewatering performance. Networks of spatially discretized wells/piezometers can be used to determine or confirm that free liquids no longer exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination/remediation technologies and diagnostic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies to eliminate free liquids include rim ditches, underdrain systems, pumping wells, manifolded extraction wellpoints, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elimination technologies are widely used and can provide diagnostic/confirmatory insights into the presence and nature of free liquids (e.g., rim ditches and open excavations enable direct observation). EPA recommends using data collected from actual dewatering efforts alongside monitoring networks when demonstrating elimination of free liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a Site Conceptual Model (CSM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elimination of free liquids relies on a well resolved understanding of site-specific geology, hydrology, and CCR material characteristics, often compiled into a Site Conceptual Model (CSM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's memorandum provides guidance on considerations for developing successful site-specific strategies to identify, measure, monitor, and eliminate free liquids and discusses elements needed to construct or augment a CSM where one does not already exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'dewatered' or 'partially dewatered' impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA distinguishes between partial dewatering (e.g., removal of standing surface water or shallow free liquids sufficient to operate equipment) and full elimination of free liquids; partial dewatering generally does not eliminate hydraulic head or the conditions that create heightened leachate risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial dewatering is an anti-pattern for claiming exemption: removing only visible surface water or free liquids to a limited depth will not remove porewater or hydraulic pressures deeper in the unit. Until free liquids are eliminated, gravity and hydraulic head can continue to drive leachate and constituent migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation places the burden on the owner or operator to demonstrate that the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) has been met; the absence of free liquids is an affirmative defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any uncertainty is construed in favor of regulation. Although EPA is not requiring posting of documentation, it recommends facilities develop and retain records to support determinations that the exception applies. EPA provided extra time in the final rule to allow facilities to determine elimination of free liquids as part of applicability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal applicability (October 19, 2015) for closed/dewatered units
rubrics_metrics.description: An impoundment that no longer contained liquid prior to October 19, 2015 would not be considered an inactive or legacy impoundment under this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cautions that merely removing visible standing water before that date ordinarily would not suffice (because lower waste may remain saturated). If a unit had been sold, regulatory obligations attach to the current owner/operator. EPA acknowledges past contamination from operations prior to dewatering and indicates other regulatory authorities (e.g., RCRA §7003, CERCLA §106) may address imminent threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of CCR landfills and CCR management units from impoundment designation
rubrics_metrics.description: A CCR landfill or CCRMU that was not designed to hold an accumulation of CCR and liquid does not become a CCR surface impoundment merely because it contains liquid (e.g., after rainfall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA looks for clear indications that the unit was not intended/designed as an impoundment, such as placement of exclusively dry CCR or construction/operation with a leachate collection and removal system meeting §257.70(d). The rule intentionally avoids blurring lines between landfills and impoundments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Paint Filter Liquids Test (PFLT) as mandatory metric
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA declined to adopt the PFLT-based definition (40 CFR 258.28(c)(1)) or otherwise mandate reliance on the Paint Filter Liquids Test for determining presence of liquids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include technical concerns about implementing the test in this context and potential sampling artifacts (vibration, heat) that could affect representativeness and produce false negatives. EPA generally would not recommend use of the PFLT in this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of the proposed technical fluid-behavior definition
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA decided not to adopt the technical definition of 'liquid' discussed in the proposal (which could categorize some bulk particulate solids as liquids because they flow), due to potential confusion (e.g., fly ash can exhibit liquid-like flow properties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considered and rejected soil-mechanics-based alternatives for defining liquid because CCR is not soil and hydraulic characterization involves considerations beyond soil physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk basis for regulating impoundments with free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Impoundments with free liquids pose significant risk because free liquids create hydraulic head and can promote leaching and contaminant migration to groundwater/aquifers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provided factual examples (e.g., units continually saturated by flowing water; units where only standing water was removed) and quantitative rainfall accumulation examples to show how precipitation can create free liquids. EPA argues that even closed/dewatered units can continue to pose unacceptable risks from contamination that occurred while operating, supporting regulation under RCRA §4004(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation and staged regulatory approach
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA limited the final rule to regulate a narrower universe (approximately 194 additional legacy surface impoundments) rather than every historical CCR impoundment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explained it is appropriate to address complex problems in stages and is not prepared to dramatically expand regulation without basic information about affected sites. EPA will continue to collect information and may use other statutory authorities where appropriate.
